source.title: Meta Dropout: Learning to Perturb Features for Generalization
source.authors: Haebeom Lee; Taewook Nam; Eunho Yang; Sung Ju Hwang

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, including appendices.
record.tranche_reason: Tests a learned latent-feature perturbation regularizer on few-shot image-classification tasks, a new setting relative to the mapped dropout claim.
record.gate_note: The paper reports held-out few-shot accuracy for MAML with and without meta-dropout and compares alternative perturbation regularizers. These results bear on V6's regularization finding, but do not test ordinary dropout, fully connected classifiers, or the stated small-data and over-regularization conditions. Cited findings are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates a new meta-learned perturbation method, not the dropout intervention specified by V6. Its learned noise generator transfers knowledge across tasks and is explicitly optimized for query performance during meta-training. Neither its performance nor comparisons with mixup and information-theoretic regularizers establish the ordinary-dropout claim. No other version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly accurate: the authors conclude that meta-dropout improves few-shot generalization and largely outperforms the tested input-dependent regularizers, while also improving adversarial robustness, less markedly on miniImageNet. These are aggregate conclusions: Meta-SGD's miniImageNet 5-shot accuracy remains 65.55, and additive meta-dropout exceeds the multiplicative version on Omniglot 5-shot.
record.recipe_differences: Uses meta-learned, input-dependent multiplicative noise on latent features during few-shot MAML or Meta-SGD adaptation; it is not ordinary dropout.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported accuracy gains vary by dataset and shot count; the 5-shot Omniglot gain is smaller than the other displayed gains. The authors also report that additive noise works well on Omniglot but is somewhat suboptimal on miniImageNet, and that learned input-dependent variance underperforms fixed variance.

fits_no_version.finding: Learned meta-dropout raises MAML accuracy in all four dataset-by-shot conditions: 95.23 to 96.63, 98.38 to 98.73, 49.58 to 51.93, and 64.55 to 67.42.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Meta-learning an input-dependent latent perturbation generator can improve few-shot adaptation on unseen image-classification tasks.

fits_no_version.finding: Selected mixup, VIB, and Information Dropout configurations reduce Omniglot 1-shot accuracy relative to unperturbed MAML.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The effects of perturbation regularizers in few-shot meta-learning depend on the regularizer and configuration.

record.problems: The results concern few-shot meta-learning on Omniglot and miniImageNet, with transductive testing via batch normalization. No random-label capacity, ordinary dropout comparison, fully connected classifier, or training/test error gap measurement is reported.
record.rows_left_out: Table 2 reports additional mixup, VIB and information-dropout settings across both datasets and shot counts. Only selected comparator rows are included; the remaining comparator settings were omitted because the mapped version concerns dropout, and these alternatives are not ordinary dropout. Table 3 ablations of noise-generator variants were also omitted because they do not test the version's ordinary-dropout claim.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance under natural versus random labels.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed to fit training data.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizers under comparable tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Ordinary dropout versus no dropout; training-set-size and excessive-dropout conditions; joint removal of dropout and weight decay with augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Removing memorized versus randomly selected training examples.

record.verdict_notes: Untested ordinary dropout is not a scope limitation demonstrated by these results. The record's V6 supports and limits_scope labels should both be removed. Few-shot adaptation also draws on extensive meta-training, so it does not directly test V6's very-small-training-set qualification.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture and local connectivity.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets.
Ordinary dropout; fully connected classifiers; the claim's small-training-set and excessive-dropout qualifications; removing dropout and weight decay together with augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to generalization gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring test accuracy.

rows.subject: MAML + Meta-dropout
rows.size_stated: 4 convolutional layers; 64 channels on Omniglot and 32 on miniImageNet
rows.operation_detail: Adds learned input-dependent multiplicative noise to latent features during inner-gradient steps.
rows.measure: Few-shot classification accuracy over 1000 randomly selected episodes.
rows.uncertainty: Standard errors for 95% confidence interval over tasks are reported.
rows.note: Authors state the reported results are average performances over 1000 episodes.
rows.check: The numbers are correct, but this is the study's own meta-dropout method versus MAML, not a test of V6's dropout intervention.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: MAML few-shot convolutional classifiers on Omniglot and miniImageNet, 1-shot and 5-shot
reader_labels.reason: Meta-dropout accuracy exceeds the no-perturbation MAML baseline in all four reported conditions (R1–R8).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The tested intervention is learned input-dependent latent-feature noise, so these results do not establish the same effect for ordinary dropout or the other regimes named in V6 (R1–R8).
